ruling: MIN-014: 读面放整个 LAN、独立只读进程、写面维持 loopback+SSH
reachableFrom: Owner machine over the LAN (192.168.51.0/24), no SSH, browser-direct
noWriteSurface: no ChainClient, no pins, no /api/chain/* routes (STORY-138); source-gated by pnpm read-face:gate
domainStore: opened read-only at the SQLite connection ({ readOnly: true })
contentSafety: CSP + nosniff + X-Frame-Options on every response; Host allow-list (anti DNS-rebinding)
vsMirrorRetirement: the retired LAN mirror was a static COPY of the cockpit on the LAN; this is the resident web served read-only by a process with no write capability — the mirror's residual use case (a LAN browser with no ssh) is now served by the read face, while D7's prohibition (network path to a pins process) is untouched because the read face has no pins
notClaimed: read-process runtime memory 'never holds pins' is unprovable by snapshot — topology + deployment-time control (MIN-014 unresolved, recorded)
no per-viewer auth by design (audience = whole LAN); content safety + no-write-surface is the boundary
cockpitData freshness follows the resident web build cadence, identical to what the Owner sees over SSH
